title: fix(spec): narrow the object designer's formula returnType options to the four declared members
body:
Fixes #19677

Clause-②: no

## The defect

`FieldSchema.returnType` declares four members — `number`, `text`, `boolean`, `date`. The object designer's quick-add grid (`packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts`, the `fields` repeater) declared an inline `options` list of **six**, adding `datetime` and `currency`. An author who added a formula field from the object designer and picked Datetime or Currency wrote a value the parse rejects.

The failure is silent at the point of choice: the select is populated from that inline list, nothing reconciles it against the enum, and the refusal arrives later from the save door naming a key the author never typed.

## The fix

Narrow the control to the four declared members. One write site, plus a regression test and a patch changeset.

This is a pull-back to a spelling that already existed in this package, not a decision about what a formula may return:

- **The enum is unchanged.** `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` is untouched — `returnType` accepted exactly these four before this change and accepts exactly these four after it. No authorable value is removed, because neither `datetime` nor `currency` was ever accepted; what is removed is an offer with nothing behind it.
- **The sibling control already spelled it correctly.** The field designer's own `returnType` select in `packages/spec/src/data/field.form.ts` carries the same explicit four-member list, with a comment saying why it is explicit. That file is untouched too. The object designer was the lone divergent carrier; three carriers now agree, counting the published reference doc (`content/docs/references/data/field.mdx`).
- **The producer side agrees with the enum.** Authoring stamps `returnType` from the inferred CEL type, and `inferExpressionType` in `@objectstack/formula` is typed `number | text | boolean | date | unknown`. There is no path by which the platform ever stamps `datetime` or `currency`, so the six-member list was never a capability that existed and got broken.

The opposite exit — widening the enum to six — was considered and rejected on that last reading. It would be a Feature and a clause-② `yes`, and nothing in the producer, the sibling control or the published docs suggests the platform means to support datetime- or currency-returning formulas.

## The regression test

`packages/spec/src/data/form-return-type-options.test.ts`, 13 assertions over both forms.

The expected set is **derived from `FieldSchema` at runtime** — read through the same JSON-Schema view the metadata-admin renderer falls back to when a row declares no `options` at all — rather than hard-coded as four strings. A test pinned to literals rots exactly the way this defect did: the enum moves, the literals do not, and the test keeps passing over a control that has drifted again.

The offer is judged at **value level**, not key level: every offered value must survive a full `safeParse` on a formula field. A key-level check would have passed on the broken grid, because `returnType` was always a recognised key.

The two removed members are additionally pinned as refused-and-unoffered. That is not a duplicate of the set equality — it is the assertion that fires if the platform ever decides a formula may return a datetime or a currency, so that the widening and the two forms move in one change.

## Verification

All commands run in a dedicated worktree at `593004aa`. Heavy runs went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`; exit codes captured before any pipe.

| command | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/spec^...' build` | exit 0 — closure empty ("No projects matched the filters"); `packages/spec` has no workspace dependencies |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` | exit 0 — 34/34 declaration files, dist stamp `e3782a80bd03` |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/data/form-return-type-options.test.ts` | exit 0 — 13 passed |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` | exit 0 — **516 files, 15056 passed**, 1 todo |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` | exit 0 — `tsc --noEmit` + scripts + test layer |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` | exit 0 — **all 15 generated artifacts up to date**; no regeneration needed |
| `pnpm lint` (repo-wide, `eslint . --no-inline-config`) | exit 0 — full population, no narrowing |
| `pnpm check:type-check-coverage` | exit 0 — 77/81 packages, test layer hides 0 files |
| 10 spec source audits (`check:empty-state`, `variant-docs`, `yaml-examples`, `exported-any`, `dual-source-exports`, `entry-nameability`, `browser-reachable-entries`, `llms-txt`, `duration-unit-keys`, `objectui-pin-citations`) | exit 0 each |
| `check:nul-bytes`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:issue-citations`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:published-files`, `check:spec-docblock-symbol-anchors` | exit 0 each |
| `check-changeset-no-major --base origin/main`, `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main`, `check-empty-changeset --base origin/main` (+ self-tests), `check:objectui-changeset`, `check:changeset-gate-self-tests` | exit 0 each |
| `pnpm check:type-check-debt` | **NOT MEASURED** — exit 3, `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`: `--re-measure` refuses without 30 workspace dependencies built. Nothing was measured, so this is neither a pass nor a finding. The ledgered packages are not in this diff. CI builds that closure before the step. |

**Reverse verification.** The fix was committed first (`3f4c20ea`), then the six-member list was reinstated on disk through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` — anchor 1 occurrence, dropping to 0; blob `38a494a2c532` moving to `ee2e9994b641`, both counted by the tool itself rather than by a claim.

The test went **red in the expected direction**: 4 of 13 failed — the set equality (`received` carrying `currency` and `datetime`), the value-level parse (`FieldSchema` answering `invalid_value` on `'datetime'`), the historical-member pin, and the two-designers agreement. The other 9 stayed green, which is the point: the derivation, the single-declaration check and the DSL-expressibility check are orthogonal to the mutation.

Restore verified by the tool on the way out: blob back to `38a494a2c532`, equal to the blob at HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` empty. No ablation artefact remains in the tree.

No `dist` preflight was needed for it: this test imports `./object.form` relative, inside its own package, so vitest resolves the source directly and no build sits between the mutation and the assertion.

## The changeset

`packages/spec` publishes this file. Measured rather than assumed: the changed `helpText` string resolves in 8 files under `packages/spec/dist`, and a positive control taken from the same source file (`Add the columns this object will store`) resolves in the same 8. `dist` is in the package's `files` whitelist, so the fix ships and takes a `patch` changeset — `skip-changeset` would have been wrong.

## Acceptance notes

- **No reconciliation gate.** Nothing mechanically holds a form's `options` list to its schema enum; both this grid and the sibling control are hand-maintained lists. The dispatch put that outside this round — a new required gate is the maintainer's call, not a rider — so the regression test covers this one key rather than the class. Noted, not filed.
- **Repo-wide, this was the only divergent carrier.** Every `returnType` occurrence under `packages/`, `content/` and `examples/` on `origin/main` was read: the six-member list existed in `object.form.ts` alone. Every other carrier already agreed with the enum.
- **Stored documents remain unmeasured**, exactly as the filer left them. Whether any authored field carries `returnType: 'datetime'` or `'currency'` today is not read here, and the fix does not depend on it either way — the parse that refuses those values is the one that already ran.
- **The objectui side is unestablished.** Whether that repo's own field designer offers the same six is outside this radius and was not read.

## Scope

Three files. `field.zod.ts` and `field.form.ts` were read-only this round and are untouched; taking either would have been the other exit.
